small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_M tiles (e.g. 256) and try BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4; the conv GEMM has M=OH*OW=64516 which is very long, so bigger M tiles reduce launch/index overhead.
- Switch the spatial tile to a 2D (BLOCK_MH × BLOCK_MW) shape so that across the K-loop, neighboring output pixels share input rows (kh,kw same), enabling the L1 to reuse loaded x_vals across the M dimension instead of recomputing gather indices per linear m.
- Drop the per-K-iter recomputation of `ic = k//(KH*KW)`, `kh`, `kw` by splitting the K loop into explicit nested loops over IC (outer, BLOCK_K_IC) and KH*KW=9 (fully unrolled constexpr), so index math is hoisted and the inner GEMM K becomes just IC.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM with the K loop ordered as `for kh: for kw: for ic_block:` and unroll kh,kw (KH=KW=3 are constexpr). This eliminates divisions/modulos inside the hot loop and lets each (kh,kw) reuse a contiguous IC-strided load pattern.
- Use a 2D output spatial tile (e.g. 16×16 or 8×32 pixels) per program so that input patches overlap heavily between neighboring outputs; combined with channels-last input layout (NHWC) the IC dimension becomes the contiguous GEMM-K and loads fully coalesce.
- Consider a persistent-CTA scheme over (N, OC tile) with the program looping over spatial tiles, amortizing weight loads (weights are only 128×576=288KB and can be tiled into SMEM once per OC tile and reused across all spatial tiles and all N).
